papers.note: A continuously refreshed coding benchmark, the working model for contamination free evaluation.
papers.title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
papers.explain_beginner: Researchers created LiveCodeBench, a new way to test how well AI language models can write code. Unlike older tests that stay the same, this benchmark continuously adds fresh coding problems from real programming competitions, preventing models from memorizing answers. The system checks not just code generation but also whether models can fix their own mistakes and predict what code will output. Testing 52 different models revealed that older benchmarks may give inflated scores because models have seen similar problems before.
papers.explain_business: Organizations selecting LLMs for coding tasks need accurate, unbiased performance metrics. LiveCodeBench provides confidence that model evaluations reflect genuine capabilities rather than memorization by continuously introducing fresh problems from actual competitions. This enables better purchasing decisions and realistic expectations for deployment. The ongoing refresh cycle means evaluations remain valid over time, reducing risk of selecting models that overperformed on outdated benchmarks but underperform in production.
papers.explain_practitioner: LiveCodeBench addresses benchmark contamination by dynamically sourcing problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces published after May 2023, ensuring evaluation data hasn't been seen during model training. The framework evaluates 52 LLMs across code generation and auxiliary capabilities including self-repair, execution, and test output prediction. The study demonstrates evidence of overfitting to existing static benchmarks and provides comprehensive empirical analysis of 18 base and 34 instruction-tuned models. Researchers will release all prompts, completions, and a toolkit for community extension.

papers.note: Position paper defining levels of contamination and calling for per benchmark measurement, widely cited in later standards work.
papers.title: NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark
papers.explain_beginner: Large language models are being tested on standard benchmark datasets to measure how well they work. However, researchers discovered a serious problem: sometimes the test data used to evaluate these models was already included in their training data. This creates fake high scores that don't reflect real performance. The paper warns that this contamination is widespread but hard to detect, leading scientists to draw wrong conclusions about which models actually work best.
papers.explain_business: Organizations relying on published LLM benchmarks to select models face a hidden risk: performance claims may be artificially inflated by data leakage rather than genuine capability. This paper identifies that standard evaluation practices lack verification mechanisms, potentially leading to poor procurement decisions. Investment in contamination detection and benchmark integrity becomes a competitive advantage, while ignoring this issue risks deploying models that underperform in real applications compared to published metrics.
papers.explain_practitioner: The authors identify data contamination as a critical validity threat in LLM evaluation, where test set exposure during training inflates benchmark performance metrics. They propose a taxonomy of contamination levels and argue for systematic per-benchmark detection mechanisms, combining automatic and semi-automatic approaches. The key finding emphasizes that contamination severity remains unmeasured across most studies, necessitating community-wide measurement protocols to prevent spurious performance claims and ensure reproducible, scientifically sound model comparisons.
